title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 12 of the notes 'Structure à l'infini des M_{g,ν}'. On the previous page Grothendieck takes a space X (think of the compactification M̄_{g,ν}) stratified by a normal-crossings divisor at infinity. He supposes that all the punctured tubular neighbourhoods D*_α of the strata are K(π,1)'s, as in the Teichmüller situation. He claims that the system of fundamental (pro)groupoids of these neighbourhoods, with their canonical maps, reconstructs two things: (i) the 'quasi-geometric' topos of sheaves on X that are locally constant on each stratum, and (ii) the homotopy types of X and of the neighbouring topoi. A marginal 'Remords' starts to qualify this. This page gives the counterexample.

The counterexample:
- Take X = P^1_C ≅ S^2 and D = {∞}, a smooth divisor reduced to a point. Then X* = C is contractible, so it is a K(π,1) with π trivial.
- The 'co-directive' system of Galois topoi attached to the stratification is D_∞ ← D*_∞ → C = X*.
- On fundamental groups this is the diagram {1} ← Z → {1}.
- The global 'quasi-galoisian' topos is the topos of sheaves on S^2 that are locally constant on the strata. Since C is simply connected, such a sheaf is constant on C.
- So the topos is the presheaf topos Ĉ on the two-object category C = (• → •). A sheaf is the same as its stalk at ∞, its generic stalk, and the specialization map between them.
- C has a final object, so its nerve is contractible. Hence H^i(Ĉ, A) = 0 for i > 0, whereas H^2(S^2) ≠ 0.
- Therefore the 1-topos of stratified-locally-constant sheaves does not have the homotopy type of X.

This leads him to the general problem: what is the homotopy type of a topos obtained by recollement (Artin gluing) of an open subtopos and its closed complement?

Modern reading:
- Set-valued constructible sheaves are functors on the exit-path category with hom-sets truncated to π_0.
- Here the exit-path space from ∞ into C is the link S^1, and π_0(S^1) = pt, which is why one gets • → •.
- The full exit-path ∞-category (Hom ≃ S^1) has groupoid completion ΣS^1 = S^2.
- Equivalently, the homotopy pushout of BZ → pt and BZ → pt is S^2.
- So the data of the K(π,1) diagram does suffice, provided it is glued homotopically (homotopy colimit, an oriented / vanishing-topos model of the punctured neighbourhood) rather than through the 1-topos recollement.

The next page begins §13, 'Digressions sur stratifications', which is presumably the start of addressing this.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. (•→•) has both an initial and a final object, so its nerve is contractible and Ĉ has trivial positive-degree cohomology with constant coefficients; H^2(S^2) ≠ 0. The counterexample is correct.
This page corrects an overstatement on the previous page: that the system of π_1's reconstructs 'les types d'homotopie des topos voisins — y compris X' through the glued sheaf topos.

Implicit nuance not stated by Grothendieck: the homotopy type of X is in fact recoverable from the same diagram {1} ← Z → {1} by taking a homotopy pushout. What fails is only the 1-topos (set-valued sheaf) recollement, which kills the link's homotopy type.

ideas.what: Topos of sheaves on a stratified space that are locally constant along strata (constructible sheaves), described as presheaves on a small category built from strata and specializations.
ideas.modern_name: Constructible sheaves ↔ representations of the exit-path category (homotopy-category truncation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, 1990s, unpublished); Treumann (2009); Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A; Barwick–Glasman–Haine (Exodromy)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§5, 'topologie modérée', dévissage of stratified structures) discusses related ideas in general terms

ideas.what: Counterexample: for S^2 stratified by a point, the constructible-sheaf topos is Ĉ with C = (•→•), which is contractible. So the 1-topos does not see the homotopy type of S^2.
ideas.modern_name: Failure of 1-truncated exit-path categories to recover homotopy type; need ∞-categorical exit paths (Hom = link ≃ S^1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; implicit in Treumann and in Lurie HA A.6, whose ∞-exit-path category has localization ≃ X

ideas.what: Reconstructing a stratified space's homotopy type from a 'co-directive' diagram of K(π,1) Galois topoi (strata ← punctured tubular neighbourhoods → open part).

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates exactly the defect later repaired by ∞-categorical exit paths. Gluing 1-topoi forgets the homotopy type of the link (here Z = π_1 of the punctured disc), so the recollement topos's homotopy type differs from that of X. He poses the general problem of computing the homotopy type of a recollement topos.
missed.quote: Cela soulève la question générale de comprendre le type d'homotopie d'un topos obtenu par "recollement" de ses ouverts et fermé complémentaire...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically it shows an early (circa 1981) recognition that stratified homotopy theory requires higher-categorical exit paths, predating MacPherson, Treumann and Lurie. Mathematically the answer is now known (∞-exit paths / Exodromy), so this is a priority and historical point rather than an open problem.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct, explicit observation that the 1-topos of constructible sheaves loses the homotopy type of the space, together with the precise reason (the Z of the link is forgotten). This anticipates the exit-path ∞-category viewpoint. It is now standard folklore, so it carries historical interest but no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'système "co-directif"' — reading appears correct ('codirectif' system of Galois topoi), i.e. a diagram indexed by the stratification poset in the 'co' direction.

The crossed/overwritten passage after 'de X = S^2' is roughly '[-à partir de-] comme un [topos] ... décrit via'; the word read as 'élast[?]' is uncertain and is probably a fragment of a deleted word, not 'élastique'.
'qui a un objet final' — correct; the category is •→•.
In the diagram, the crossed-out target under the arrow from D*_∞ is a scribbled-over 'C', replaced by 'C = P^1_C \ {∞} = X*'.
